sections.heading: Introduction
paras: Beyond the big three (performance, reliability, usability) sit security, interoperability, localisation and accessibility — each with its own lecture slide and a standing invitation in Worksheet 4 Q5. The 2022 paper's finale (Q3.4d) asks you to propose one such parameter for the patient monitor, justify it, and write its requirement: 6 marks for judgement plus craft.

bullets: Security — everyone's responsibility: authentication, authorisation, audit. Vitals are health data; unauthorised display or alteration harms patients.
Interoperability — software must work with other software: export vitals to the hospital EHR in an agreed format.
Localisation (L10N) — adapt language, units, culture: ward staff across campuses need consistent units and terminology.
Accessibility — cater for diverse abilities: alarms perceivable by staff with hearing or vision limits; operable gloved and one-handed.
sections.heading: The four, briefly
paras: Exam move in two steps: (1) parameter + reason tied to the system ('security, because vitals are confidential health data on a shared ward display'); (2) quantified requirement ('the system shall lock the display after 60 s idle and require badge re-authentication; unauthorised access attempts shall be logged with timestamp and user ID'). Judgement first, numbers second.

summary: Security, interoperability, localisation and accessibility complete the NFR palette — propose the parameter that fits the system's risks, then quantify it.
title: Security, interoperability, localisation, accessibility
